steps.text: Plantain (80/120 g) peeled and sliced 1.5 cm thick on the diagonal. Griddle or heavy pan, DRY, high. 3 minutes a side until blackened in patches. Set aside and salt.
Same pan, rapeseed oil (5/6 g), medium-high. Onion (40/50 g) and pepper (80/100 g), diced, 4 minutes.
Tomato (100/120 g) chopped, plus scotch bonnet to taste and a pinch of stock powder. Cook 4–5 minutes, pressing it down, until it darkens and the oil separates at the edges.
Beat the eggs (150/175 g — 3 / 3½) loosely. Pour in, leave 20 seconds, then draw through in slow ribbons. Off the heat while still glossy.
Spinach (60/80 g) folded through on the residual heat.

why: Wait for the oil to separate before the eggs go in. That's the moment the tomato stops being raw and the sauce gets its depth — go early and the whole thing tastes thin and slightly metallic.
notes: D0-003: the pan-frying oil (single hot-pan use, softening onion/pepper) becomes rapeseed_oil.
